data.title: Pyrazinamide (PZA)
data.summary: Antituberculous drugs · Nicotinamide analogue; first-line antituberculous drug
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Antituberculous drugs_

**Class:** Nicotinamide analogue; first-line antituberculous drug

## Mechanism of action
- Prodrug converted by mycobacterial pyrazinamidase to pyrazinoic acid, which is active in acidic environments (inside macrophages and caseous lesions)
- Disrupts membrane energy and trans-translation → kills semi-dormant bacilli — key to the 6-month short-course regimen

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Intensive phase of TB treatment (first 2 months), including cutaneous TB
- Not effective against M. bovis (naturally resistant) — relevant for BCG complications

## Dose & formulations
- 25 mg/kg/day (range 20–30) in fixed-dose combinations

## Adverse effects
- Hepatotoxicity (dose-related) — the most hepatotoxic first-line drug at high doses
- Hyperuricaemia and gout (inhibits urate excretion); arthralgia
- Photosensitivity, rash, pruritus; GI upset

## Contraindications
- Severe liver disease; acute gout

## Drug interactions
- Antagonises probenecid and allopurinol (raises uric acid)

## Monitoring
- LFT; uric acid if joint symptoms

## Pregnancy & lactation
WHO recommends its use in pregnancy (US guidance more cautious).

## Viva points
- Works in acid pH — kills intracellular, semi-dormant bacilli
- Hyperuricaemia; M. bovis/BCG is naturally resistant

_Sources: Khopkar ch.7; Wolverton 4e ch.9. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
